# Verified Elsewhere — resolving a video against a source we do not plug into

> ⚠️ **Approved 2026-08-17 at the Human Operator's direction.** Raised from use: the wired source is incomplete, and a video the operator has personally verified against a real listing elsewhere is indistinguishable from one nobody has looked at.
> 
> 🚨 **This spec names no source, and neither may the code.** Per the Plugin Architecture epic D7/D9 the public repository must never name a metadata source. The operator will type one in; core treats it as free text and never enumerates. Every example below is therefore written as *"a source we do not plug into"*.
## Intention
The app models two states: **matched by a provider**, or **unmatched**. There is no third, and the third is the common case — a record the operator has resolved by reading a listing in their own browser.
Today that work is discarded. The video stays in the lookup queue, re-appears in every audit, and the next batch run asks the same question that already failed.
### 📊 Measured, drive library 2026-08-17
| State | Count |
| --- | --- |
| matched | 1,414 |
| noMatch | 500 |
| ambiguous | 159 |
| unmatchable | 4 |
⭐ Of the 663 unmatched, **535 already carry cast** and **426 a studio**. These are not empty records. They are records with nowhere to be confirmed.
⚠️ The **159 ambiguous** are a different problem and are NOT in scope: the source returned candidates and nobody chose. That is disambiguation, which *Match Confidence* and the doubtful-match queue address. This spec is about the **500** the source has no record of at all.
## 🔴 D1 — The machinery exists; a screen does not
Every field is already there, and this is the whole reason the spec is small:
| Field | Already means |
| --- | --- |
| `enrichmentSource` | free text — core never enumerates sources |
| `enrichmentSourceId` | that source's own reference |
| `enrichmentUrl` | the page, checkable by a person |
| `MatchMethod.operator` | entered or confirmed by a person |
And three consequences already fall out, **verified against the code rather than assumed**:
- `VideoBatchPolicy.skipReason` returns *"already matched"*, so it leaves the lookup queue
- `matchesToRecheck(source:)` filters `WHERE source = ?`, so an unwired source is never re-checked by the wired one's audit
- *Match Confidence* C6 is fingerprints only, so an operator match is correctly never doubted
## 🚨 D2 — Inbound only, and it must never quietly become otherwise
The operator reads a page in their own browser and types what they found. **No request leaves the device.** `ProviderBoundary` is therefore not involved — there is nothing to refuse, because nothing is sent.
⚠️ Stated as a decision rather than as a description, because a feature named after an external source invites the assumption that it talks to one. It does not, and acquiring that ability later is a new decision with a privacy boundary attached, not an enhancement.
## D3 — A statement outranks evidence, as everywhere else
🔴 A later automated run must not overwrite what the operator entered. Same rule as the hand-set studio parent and the hand-set content kind: evidence does not overwrite a statement.
## ⚠️ D4 — A link is a link
A reference the operator cannot open is worth nothing. A value that is not a URL is **refused at entry** rather than stored as an unusable string — the failure otherwise surfaces months later as a dead row nobody can check.
## D5 — Reversible
Clearing it returns the video to the queue and leaves no orphaned reference. A half-cleared record — no state but a lingering source id — is exactly what a later run reads as evidence of a match.
## Test strategy
- **V1** — a recorded source, reference and link takes the video out of the lookup queue
- **V2** — 🚨 it is not re-checked by the wired source's stale-match audit
- **V3** — 🔴 a later automated run does not overwrite the operator's values
- **V4** — the source name is free text; nothing in core enumerates sources
- **V5** — 🚨 no outbound request is made by any part of this path
- **V6** — clearing it returns the video to the queue and leaves no orphaned reference
- **V7** — a link that is not a URL is refused rather than stored
## ❓ Open — Human Operator
1. **Should a second automated provider be built as well?** A real API exists for at least one other source and the plugin architecture already supports many — the registry holds several and the app names none, so it is a new package rather than a change to ViLM. 🔴 **Recommend deciding separately, after this ships.** This covers the same need for *any* source at a fraction of the cost and with no terms-of-service question, and it will also show how often the manual path is actually reached — which is the number that should decide whether a second provider is worth maintaining.
2. Should a manually verified video be **visually distinct** in the grid from an automatically matched one, or is the source name in the inspector enough?
